claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you find out if you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you a few questions about your circumstances.

First of all, could you please tell me how many children you'd like to claim Child Benefit for, and what are their names and ages?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! I'm looking to claim for my son Alex. He's 17 years old.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for letting me know about Alex. Since he's 17 years old, I have a few more questions to determine your eligibility.

Is Alex currently in approved education or training (such as A-levels, NVQs, or a similar course)? Or has he left education/training?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he's not in any education or training at the moment. He left school and isn't studying anything right now.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. Since Alex is 17 and not currently in approved education or training, I have a couple more questions:

Has Alex registered with either a government-sponsored careers service or the armed services since leaving education?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he hasn't registered with any careers service or the armed forces. He just left school and hasn't signed up for anything like that.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying. I have one more important question:

Is Alex currently working 24 hours or more per week, or receiving any benefits in his own right (such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance)?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he's not working at all right now, and he doesn't receive any benefits in his own name either.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. I just have a couple more questions about your own circumstances:

Do you live in the UK, and do you live with Alex or contribute towards his upkeep (for example, food, clothes, or pocket money)?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK and Alex lives at home with me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you. Just one more question to complete the assessment:

Do you have the right to live in the UK (for example, are you a British or Irish citizen, do you have settled status, or another form of immigration status that allows you to reside here)?

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Thank you for providing all that information. I now have enough details to assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Based on the information you've provided, I'm afraid **you are not currently eligible for Child Benefit for Alex**.

Here's why:

**For Alex (age 17):**
- Child Benefit normally ends when a child turns 16 unless they remain in approved education or training (such as A-levels, NVQs, or similar qualifications).
- Since Alex has left school and is not currently in any approved education or training, he doesn't meet this requirement.
- There is an option to continue receiving Child Benefit for up to **20 weeks** if a 16 or 17-year-old registers with either a government-sponsored careers service or the armed services after leaving education. However, Alex has not registered with either of these.

**What you could do:**
If Alex decides to:
1. **Return to approved education or training** – you could then claim Child Benefit until he turns 20 (as long as he remains in approved education/training), or
2. **Register with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed services** – you may be able to claim Child Benefit for up to 20 weeks from when he left education.

I hope this helps clarify your situation. If Alex's circumstances change, you may wish to reassess your eligibility at that time.

For children aged 16 or over, Child Benefit can normally only continue if the child stays in approved education or training (until they turn 20). Alternatively, Child Benefit can continue for 20 weeks if a 16 or 17 year old leaves education or training and registers with either a government-sponsored careers service or the armed services. Alex has not registered with either of these services. Since Alex is over 16, not in approved education or training, and has not registered with a careers service or the armed forces, the eligibility criteria for Child Benefit are not met.
